nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Reforestation initiatives|Riverine habitat restoration_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the main focus of the study conducted by Munyai and colleagues?
nodes.answer: The study focused on assessing the macroinvertebrate community structure in relation to water and sediment chemistry in a subtropical African river system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Reforestation initiatives|Riverine habitat restoration_qna_001
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What habitats were sampled along the transect?
nodes.answer: The habitats sampled included pools, bedrock, littoral/riparian vegetation/macrophytes, stones in current, stones out of current, rapids/riffles, gravel, sand, and mud.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Reforestation initiatives|Riverine habitat restoration_qna_002
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What challenge is highlighted regarding hydromorphological restoration despite advances in wastewater treatment?
nodes.answer: The challenge is that hydromorphological restoration often falls short of achieving ecological recovery despite substantial advances in water quality.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Reforestation initiatives|Riverine habitat restoration_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of empirical studies support the shifts from abiotic to biotic controls in community structure?
nodes.answer: Empirical studies examining the influence of abiotic and biotic factors on stream macroinvertebrate communities and the role of connectivity and seasonality in stream restoration support these shifts.
